sections.label: Children and Young Persons Act
sections.summary: The Children and Young Persons Act provides for the welfare, care, protection and rehabilitation of children below 16 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These families need a lot of support and intervention, to make sure the children have the best shot in life in spite of their circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is where the Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) comes in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It provides for the welfare, care, protection and rehabilitation of children and young persons below 16 years of age, whom I will subsequently refer to collectively as "children".

sections.label: Raising age limit for young person
sections.summary: Clause 2 raises the age limit for "young person" and "juvenile" to cover children below 18 so intervention is possible when older children's safety is threatened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clause 2 amends the definition of "young person" and "juvenile" to raise the age limit to cover children below the age of 18 so that we can intervene when the safety of older children is threatened.

sections.label: Defining emotional harm
sections.summary: Clauses 2 and 4 of the Bill define emotional harm, including manifestations such as delayed development or post-traumatic stress disorder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To address this, clauses 2 and 4 of the Bill define emotional harm, which includes manifestations, such as delayed development or post-traumatic stress disorder.

sections.label: Day-to-day care decisions
sections.summary: Clause 41 allows MSF and designated caregivers to make day-to-day care decisions for children under a Care and Protection order without parental consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clause 41 allows MSF and designated caregivers to make day-to-day care decisions for children under a Care and Protection order without the need for parental consent.

sections.label: Enhanced Care and Protection Order
sections.summary: Clause 41 enables the Court to place children under an Enhanced Care and Protection Order up till age 21, letting MSF and caregivers make day-to-day and substantive decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We should do what we can to provide them with a sense of stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 41 of the Bill enables the Court to place such children under a new Enhanced Care and Protection Order (ECPO) up till the age of 21.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The ECPO allows MSF and designated caregivers to make day-to-day, as well as more substantive decisions, such as overseas travel, just as what parents would do in normal family settings.

sections.label: Foster parents authorising treatment
sections.summary: The new ECPO allows foster parents, with MSF's authorisation and in consultation with medical practitioners, to decide more timely for Ben's treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The new ECPO will allow the foster parents, with MSF's authorisation and in consultation with medical practitioners, to make a more timely decision to allow Ben to be treated.

sections.label: Childcare leave for foster parents
sections.summary: Foster parents who answered MSF's call for family-based care are to receive childcare leave benefits like natural parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These foster parents have responded to MSF's call for more people to step forward to provide family-based care in lieu of institutional care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We seek Parliament's support to grant childcare leave benefits to our foster parents to enable and help them with caregiving challenges that they face, just as natural parents do.

sections.label: Youth Court jurisdiction age raised
sections.summary: Clause 2 expands the Youth Court's jurisdiction to hear cases involving youth offenders below 18, up from 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, clause 2 expands the jurisdiction of the Youth Court to hear cases involving youth offenders below 18, up from the current 16.

sections.label: Probation willingness age raised
sections.summary: Clause 71 lets the Youth Court impose probation on a child below 18 without willingness, raising the minimum age from 14 to 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, clause 71 makes related amendments to the Probation of Offenders Act, to enable the Youth Court to impose probation on a child below the age of 18, even if they do not express willingness to comply with the conditions of probation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Currently, the Youth Court must ask a child who is 14 years old and above if he is willing to comply with the terms of probation, before it imposes such an order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will raise the minimum age from 14 to 18.

sections.label: JRC detention and restraints
sections.summary: Clause 32 lets the Youth Court decide on JRC detention for offenders aged 14 to below 18, and clause 48 allows restraints in Youth Homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clause 32, therefore, allows the Youth Court to decide if an offender aged 14 to below 18 can be safely detained at a JRC and, if not, the Court may make an order for the offender to undergo Reformative Training in the first instance without going through a JRC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To further enhance safety and security in MSF's Youth Homes, clause 48 allows MSF officers working in the Homes to use restraints, such as handcuffs, leg braces and flexicuffs, to prevent incidents of escape, self-injury or injury to others.

sections.label: Spent records for youth offenders
sections.summary: Clause 73 amends the Registration of Criminals Act so a youth offender's record is spent after completing his Youth Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is why the Yellow Ribbon project is incredibly important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We, therefore, propose to amend the Registration of Criminals Act via clause 73 of the Bill so that a youth offender's criminal record will be considered spent once he successfully completes his Youth Court order.

sections.label: Family Guidance Order replaces BPC
sections.summary: The BPC label is replaced by the Family Guidance Order, requiring parents and child to complete a family programme before a Court application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: However, many social work professionals, legal practitioners and my own MSF colleagues have shared with me that it is just as, if not more important, to address poor parent-child relationships and poor or absent parenting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will, therefore, do away with the label BPC and replace it with a new order known as the Family Guidance Order (FGO), which makes clear that our focus is on the role of and dynamics within the family and not just squarely looking at the behaviour of the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The new framework requires parents and child to complete a family programme before the parents can file for a Court application.

sections.label: Family guidance order age threshold
sections.summary: For FGOs the current age threshold stays, so a parent can apply for family guidance only if the child is below 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For FGOs, however, there will be no change to the current age threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This means that a parent can make a Court application for family guidance only if their child is below 16 years of age.

sections.label: Clauses 7 and 51 partners
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 51 strengthen partners' roles with statutory support, legal protection and relevant information sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Clauses 7 and 51 of the Bill strengthen the roles of these partners by providing them with appropriate statutory support and legal protection, as well as enabling relevant information sharing.

sections.label: Clause 51 legal liability protection
sections.summary: Clause 51 extends protection from legal liability to people performing functions under the Act who acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The conflicts within families can create acrimony that poses risk to people who work to support them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Thus, clause 51 extends to people performing a function or exercising powers under the Act protection from legal liability, as long as they have acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

sections.label: Extending Act to older youths
sections.summary: The amendments extend the Act to abused or neglected children and young offenders aged 16 to below 18, though stakeholders raised concerns about the wide age range.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The amendments to extend the Act to include children who are abused or neglected and young offenders aged 16 to below 18 are, therefore, a good move.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I would like to echo the concerns of some stakeholders about the implications of having to oversee and rehabilitate a wide age range of children and young people.

sections.label: Sector capability for older youths
sections.summary: The member asks whether the problem will be aggravated by a wider age group and what the Ministry assesses about the sector's capability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Will this problem be aggravated when there is a wider age group of residents, with older youths?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, what is the Ministry's assessment of the capability of the sector to carry out the necessary functions to manage a higher number of children and young people?

sections.label: Section 68A mechanical restraint clarification
sections.summary: The member seeks clarification on the proposed section 68A allowing a person-in-charge of a Government-operated home to use or authorise mechanical restraint.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to seek a clarification on the proposed amendment to include the new section 68A, which enables the person-in-charge of any home for children and young persons that is operated by or under the management or control of the Government to use or authorise any person who is assisting the person-in-charge to use mechanical restraint on a person detained in the home.

sections.label: Questions on group home provision
sections.summary: An MP asks what considerations led to the provision, what standard operating procedures guide the power, and what checks prevent abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that the Minister has earlier explained the need to ensure safety of the social workers as well as other residents who are in the group home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I would like to understand these specific considerations that led to the decision to have this provision and how we could reconcile the spirit of rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, I would also like to know what standard operating procedures are in place to guide the use of this power and what processes and checks are in place to prevent the abuse of this provision.

sections.label: Support for CYPA age amendment
sections.summary: An MP supports the Bill and the amendment raising the maximum age for protection under the CYPA to 18 from 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the comments I made earlier, I stand in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Specifically, I would like to restate my support for the amendment which will raise the maximum age for protection under the CYPA to 18, up from the current age of 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have been tracking this issue for some time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that when the Bill comes into force, youths aged between 16 and 18 who face criminal charges will, in general, be tried in the Youth Court, which sits in private and in an atmosphere of greater understanding, compared to the open adult Courts.

sections.label: Clause 25 production within 48 hours
sections.summary: Clause 25 proposes amending section 30(2) to add that the youth should be produced before the Magistrate within 48 hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 25 proposes to amend section 30(2) to add that the youth should be produced before the Magistrate "within 48 hours".

sections.label: Clause 27 adult Court trial
sections.summary: Under clause 27, youths can be tried in an adult Court if the offence is in the new Second Schedule or the accused was previously found guilty of a similar offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under clause 27, such youths can be tried in an adult Court if the offence involved is listed in the new Second Schedule, or if the accused has been found guilty of a similar offence previously.

sections.label: Discretion of Youth Court power
sections.summary: An MP asks the Minister to reconfirm that the power in the Youth Court and the Public Prosecutor is discretionary, so a case may remain in the Youth Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister reconfirm that the power in the Youth Court and the Public Prosecutor is discretionary, that is to say, such a case may still remain in the Youth Court?

sections.label: Clause 32 first-time RT
sections.summary: Clause 32 introduces a new category where a Youth Court could order RT for a youth being sentenced for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, clause 32 introduces a new category where a Youth Court could order RT for a youth who is being sentenced for the first time.

sections.label: Replacing BPC with FGO
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes clause 43, which replaces BPC orders with FGO, a more nurturing term that does not blame the child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Children under BPC are effectively labelled as "bad" children and will undergo psychological damage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I thus welcome clause 43 of the Bill, which replaces the existing BPC orders with FGO, a more nurturing term that does not blame the child.

sections.label: Costs of complying with programmes
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify who will pay the costs of complying with programmes that involve interfacing with professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such programmes involve interfacing with professionals, could the Minister clarify who will pay the costs of complying with these requirements?

sections.label: Form before hearing and abuse cases
sections.summary: The speaker suggests giving persons a form before their hearing, supports the Bill, and notes rising reported abuse cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a second alternative, can there be a simple process of, say, a form being given out to these persons ahead of their hearing, so that they have time to formulate their thoughts and write them out for the Court to follow more easily?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The changes in this Bill are, overall, steps in the right direction and bring our law in line with international norms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I support the Bill and look forward to the Ministry's responses to my queries.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What is worrying is that the number of cases being reported has been on the rise, especially for sexual abuse with 248 cases, up from 107 in 2016 and 181 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Physical abuse at 584 cases, up from 444 in 2016, 373 in 2017.

sections.label: Aim of the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill aims to strengthen Government and community support to help these children and improve their rehabilitation and reintegration into society.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The aim of this Bill is to strengthen the Government and community support to help these children and improve their rehabilitation and reintegration into society.

sections.label: Parenting education clinic proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSF can run a parenting education clinic or structured programme for parents of primary or secondary school children.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am very encouraged to read of how a number of cases of sexual abuse were captured by MOE after the students went through lessons on sex education and spoke to the counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, for MSF, can a parenting education clinic be run for parents who need to address the challenges they face in bringing up their child, perhaps some form of structured programme for parents who have children in primary or secondary school?

sections.label: MSF child abuse investigations rise
sections.summary: MSF investigated 272 child abuse cases involving family members in 2009, 381 in 2014, and 1,163 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, in 2009, MSF investigated 272 cases of child abuse involving family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Fast forward five years, in 2014, MSF investigated 381 such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By 2018, MSF investigated 1,163 in one year alone.

sections.label: Definition of young persons
sections.summary: Clause 2(1)(b) and 2(2)(b) amend the definition of young persons, extending the Act from 16 years and below to 18 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 2(1)(b) and 2(2)(b) amends the definition of young persons, extending the applicability of the Act from those 16 years of age and below to those 18 and below.

sections.label: Child abuse within family
sections.summary: The Bill addresses child abuse within the family, particularly when state intervention in the parent-child relationship is in the child's best interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Fourthly and ultimately, Sir, this Bill addresses child abuse within the family, particularly tackling the question at what point is it in the best interests of the child or young person that the state intervenes in the parent-child relationship?

sections.label: Discretion of Child Protection Officers
sections.summary: Broader discretion given to Child Protection Service Officers must achieve deterrence of child abuse and come with powers to act swiftly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even as we seek to find a better balance, we must also ensure that the broader discretion given to Child Protection Service Officers achieves deterrence of child abuse, and that deterrence must come with powers to act swiftly.

sections.label: Resources, training, emotional harm, restraints
sections.summary: The passage asks about resources and manpower for officers' discretion, childcare teacher training, emotional harm as ill-treatment, and proposed mechanical restraints on children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would the Minister elaborate on whether there are sufficient resources, particularly manpower, to exercise that broad discretion given to the officers in light of the unfortunately increasing number of cases investigated as well as the expansion in definition of child abuse through this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As a significant number of child abuse cases involve children under the tender age of seven, would the Minister also elaborate on how childcare teachers have been trained to be able to detect child abuse?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, I am especially heartened that the Bill now includes emotional harm as a form of ill-treatment, thereby allowing affected children and young persons to be protected by the Bill and allows older youth offenders to have more rehabilitative options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And yet, in the very same Bill that recognises emotional harm as a form of ill-treatment, a new section 68A proposes the use of mechanical restraints on children and young persons. "Mechanical restraints" in this case refer to handcuffs, leg braces, flexicuffs or any similar means of restraint.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2008 research by Cornell University found restraints to be "a considerable risk to vulnerable youths, are intrusive, have a negative effect on the treatment environment, and have a profound effect on those youths who have experienced trauma in their lives." It is also not clear to me if there are any guidelines on its use, or if restraints should only be used after less intrusive methods have been applied and deemed ineffective, especially when there are already therapeutic and trauma-informed alternatives as well as environmental interventions available, such as a padded room to prevent self-harm or a Calming Room to manage aggressive/violent behaviour.

sections.label: Contact and family reunification
sections.summary: Research on family reunification shows maintaining parent or family-child contact in the first six months of alternative care placement improves reunification chances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Research on family reunification shows maintaining parent/family-child contact in the first six months of alternative care placement improves the chances of family reunification.

sections.label: Tiered foster care system
sections.summary: The passage urges the Ministry to consider a tiered foster care system with tiered allowances based on the complexities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Second, I urge the Ministry to consider a tiered foster care system with tiered allowances based on the complexities.

sections.label: Tax relief for foster carers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes tax relief for foster carers as recognition, retention and an incentive for more families to apply, citing Australian tax exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Next, I would like to propose tax relief for foster carers as a means of recognition and retention as well as an incentive for more potential families to apply to the fostering scheme, as how the Australian government has incorporated tax exemptions into their fostering provisions.

sections.label: Teenage suicides and SOS calls
sections.summary: A record number of teenage boys committed suicide in 2018, and SOS calls from children aged five to nine rose 500% in three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: A record number of teenage boys committed suicide in 2018 according to the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS), and calls to SOS by children between five and nine have jumped by an alarming 500% within three years.

sections.label: Programmes based on offending behaviours
sections.summary: Programmes and interactions by Social Service Agencies, schools and grassroots are currently designed based on offending behaviours, not risk factors such as mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Currently, the programmes and interactions for children and young persons by Social Service Agencies, schools and grassroots are designed based on offending behaviours and not on the risk factors, such as mental health conditions.

sections.label: Protection extended to ages 17 and 18
sections.summary: With the change, this protection will be extended to children aged 17 and 18.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the change, this protection will be extended to children aged 17 and 18.

sections.label: Singaporean children's first Internet device
sections.summary: A Google survey found Singaporean children get their first Internet-connected device at age eight, below the global average of 10.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, a Google survey found that Singaporean children get their first Internet-connected device at the age of eight, below the global average of 10, making them among the youngest in the world to go online.

sections.label: VTech fined for children's privacy
sections.summary: In January 2018, American toy company VTech was fined $650,000 by the US Federal Trade Commission for failing to protect children's privacy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In January 2018, American electronic toy company VTech was fined $650,000 by the US Federal Trade Commission for failing to protect the privacy of children using its gadgets.

sections.label: Children's data collection by companies
sections.summary: As children use digital devices younger, companies must face requirements for greater care and transparency in data collection, especially for children.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As children are using digital devices at ever younger ages, we need to hold companies to task for their data collection processes, especially those pertaining to children, by introducing requirements for greater care and transparency in their practices.

sections.label: Instagram head meets British Health Secretary
sections.summary: In February, Instagram head Adam Mosseri met British Health Secretary Matt Hancock to discuss measures on content promoting self-harm and suicide.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In February this year, Instagram head Adam Mosseri met with the British Health Secretary Matt Hancock to discuss new measures the company would introduce to handle content promoting self-harm and suicide.

sections.label: Instagram self-harm content and local survey
sections.summary: Instagram pledged to identify self-harm content and hide it behind sensitivity screens; a YouGov survey found a third of young adults here have self-harmed.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instagram has since pledged to better identify content relating to self-harm and hide it behind "sensitivity screens".

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Closer to home, a survey by international research agency YouGov found that a third of young adults here have self-harmed, with one in 10 doing so frequently.

sections.label: UN discussion on children's digital rights
sections.summary: A 2014 UN committee discussion concluded States should adopt a national coordinating framework for children's rights and digital media; the speaker urges Singapore to do so.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2014, the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child held a Day of General Discussion on digital media and children’s rights.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It concluded that "States should adopt a national coordinating framework with a clear mandate and sufficient authority to coordinate all activities related to children’s rights and digital media and information and communications technology at cross-sectoral, national, regional and local levels and facilitate international cooperation." Given our whole-of-Government approach to tackling our national priorities, I believe that protecting and advancing children’s digital rights with a national coordinating framework are a task Singapore should actively undertake.

sections.label: Replacing emotional injury with emotional harm
sections.summary: The speaker supports clause 4 replacing "emotional injury" with "emotional harm", as harm is more all-encompassing and may not be visible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, I would like to speak on clause 4 which amends section 4 of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support replacing "emotional injury" with "emotional harm". "Injury" tends to suggest that the abuse is rather tangible or explicit and is visible, while "harm" is more all-encompassing and suggests that while it may not necessarily be visible, the damage the abuse has caused is much more far-reaching and may manifest itself in ways other than that which is visible.

sections.label: Emotional abuse amendments and fostering committee
sections.summary: The speaker supports amendments to section 4 on emotional or psychological abuse and the formation of the Committee on Fostering for young persons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some suffer in silence while some start to develop a facade of indifference, while some of these emotionally or physically abused children would, in turn, inflict pain on others who are in a position more vulnerable than they are, such as a younger sibling or a classmate or schoolmate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the amendments to section 4 to expand and set out the circumstances in which a child or young person may be regarded as being subject to emotional or psychological abuse and would need care or protection beyond that which can be given by their biological parents or legal guardians.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to speak on the fostering of young persons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am supportive of the formation of the Committee on Fostering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe this will help provide a more objective and fairer platform for the review of foster care to be provided to young persons who have to be removed from the care of their biological parents or even foster parents.

sections.label: Fostering rules and Committee
sections.summary: The speaker says clause 23 inserts a new Part IIA on Fostering, setting rules and a Committee on Fostering appointed by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is unfortunate that when a foster care case does not turn out the way that the foster parents or even biological parents expect, it is somehow expedient to blame MSF and the MSF officers working on the case for it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I feel that the insertion of clause 23 in the Bill to include a new Part IIA on Fostering will be useful in delineating the rules and provisions for fostering, particularly in setting up a Committee on Fostering made up of individuals appointed by the Minister who may be able to provide inputs and opinions from a seemingly more neutral and balanced perspective.

sections.label: Foster parent leave and restraint
sections.summary: The speaker supports extending childcare, extended childcare and unpaid infant care leave to foster parents, and seeks clarification on clause 48's mechanical restraint provision.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to state my support for childcare leave, extended childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave to be extended to foster parents who have opened up their hearts and homes to these vulnerable children and young persons in need of love and care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One aspect of this Bill that I would like to seek clarifications on is clause 48 with the introduction of section 68A.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am somewhat concerned with the provision to allow the person-in-charge of any home for children and young persons, or any other authorised persons in that home, to use a mechanical restraint on a person detained in the home, called a detainee, in order to prevent the detainee from escaping from custody, or to prevent the detainee from inflicting any bodily injury on themselves or on others.

sections.label: Government initiatives like M3
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government has implemented initiatives such as M3, combining efforts, manpower and funds from MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Even so, we should acknowledge that various initiatives have been implemented by the Government to overcome the community’s challenges or issues, such as the establishment of M3 which involves the combination of efforts, manpower and also funds from the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), the Council on Education for Muslim Children (MENDAKI) and the People’s Association Malay Activity Executive Committees Council (MESRA), which comprise grassroots organisations and efforts by volunteers.

sections.label: MSF consultation numbers
sections.summary: MSF consulted over 300 stakeholders in the children and youth services sector and considered over 40 written responses in the public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MSF consulted over 300 stakeholders in the children and youth services sector and considered over 40 written responses during the public consultation.

sections.label: Staff-to-children ratio at places of safety
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for the current staff-to-children ratio at places of safety and whether MSF has studied the optimum ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what the current staff is to children ratio is at the "places of safety"?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if MSF has studied the optimum staff is to children ratio?

sections.label: Siblings not separated in places of safety
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Minister will consider adopting the policy that siblings should not be separated where possible when deciding where children go to a place of safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider adopting the same policy position that siblings should not be separated where possible when making decisions about where children go when sent to a "place of safety"?

sections.label: Data on children in places of safety
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it collects data on children who enter a place of safety and later enter boys' or girls' homes and prisons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share if it collects data on how many children who enter a "place of safety" later enter the boys' or girls' homes and, later on, even prisons?

sections.label: Tracking effectiveness of places of safety
sections.summary: A boy in a place of safety was caught housebreaking and sent to a boys' home, and the Ministry is urged to track the effectiveness of places of safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While in a "place of safety", he was caught housebreaking and was sent to a boys' home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to track and study the effectiveness of our "place of safety".

sections.label: Mechanical restraints in children's homes
sections.summary: New section 68A allows persons-in-charge of homes for children and young persons to use mechanical restraints such as handcuffs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, the new section 68A allows persons-in-charge of homes for children and young persons to use mechanical restraints, such as handcuffs.

sections.label: Increasing Auxiliary Officers for separation
sections.summary: The question asks whether separation can be maintained by increasing Auxiliary Officers so MSF staff do not take on this role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can we maintain this separation by increasing the number of Auxiliary Officers, if necessary, so that the MSF staff do not have to take on this role?

sections.label: Children in home-based care
sections.summary: The question asks how many children are currently in home-based care, including Government and VWO-based orphanages and boys' and girls' homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On average, how many of our children are currently based in home-based care, such as Government and VWO-based orphanage, as well as in boys' and girls' homes?

sections.label: Adoption cost for sandwich class
sections.summary: Free legal aid exists for the needy, but adoption costs thousands of dollars, a big cost to the sandwich class trying to adopt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the needy, there is of course the free legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But adoption cost goes into thousands of dollars and this is a big cost to the sandwich class who are trying to adopt.

sections.label: Mandatory therapy for online addiction
sections.summary: Speaker hopes MSF and MOE's compulsory education unit explore mandatory therapy for youths in extreme online addiction circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But I would like to see whether there is a systematic way where we can deal with this emerging issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that MSF and the compulsory education unit within MOE can work together to explore whether, in extreme and only extreme circumstances, can we put the children and our youths into mandatory therapy to deal with this online addiction.

sections.label: Online addiction and children's welfare
sections.summary: Speaker says online addiction can compromise a child's future and thanks MSF and VWOs; the Bill frames welfare, care, protection and rehabilitation of at-risk children and young persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One may argue that this may not constitute as severe self-harm in the traditional sense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But in this day and age, if a child or young person is not able even to complete his basic education due to online addiction, in my view, I believe his or her future will be seriously compromised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I would also like to thank MSF and the officers from the various VWOs for their tireless work to care for our vulnerable children and youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is an important Bill because it sets the framework to better provide for the welfare, care, protection and rehabilitation of children and young persons (CYPs) at risk in our midst.

sections.label: Integrated turnkey solution with case manager
sections.summary: Speaker calls for an integrated turnkey solution coordinated by an appointed lead case manager that all relevant parties can turn to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Fourthly, and most important of all, the need for an integrated "turnkey" solution properly coordinated by an appointed lead case manager, a solution integrator of sorts that all relevant parties helping the children and these young persons, the relevant parties, can turn to.

sections.label: More resources for care coordination
sections.summary: With the foster mother aging and having cancer, the speaker feels more resources should go to MSF to strengthen coordination and integration of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As his foster mother ages and is having cancer, there is not enough confidence amongst all the parties working with him that there is a good transition and handshake.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, I feel there is a strong need to invest more resources to MSF to strengthen the coordination and integration of care.

sections.label: Young persons' voice and foster parents
sections.summary: Speaker seeks clarification on strengthening young persons' voices, welcomes foster parents as key partners, and suggests wider recruitment, more case management involvement and more training and support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek clarification from the Ministry on how the voice of these young persons can be sought and strengthened in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am pleased that foster parents are officially added in this Bill as key partners to support children and young persons in need of protection and rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Foster parents, if properly selected and trained, provide a more natural and desirable setting than a group home for these young people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I have studied the Ministry’s Fostering Scheme and found it to be useful and structured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, to cast the net wider to attract more suitable and interested foster parent candidates; two, to involve them more in the case management process so as to better integrate the care across schools, foster home and other areas; and three, to put in more resources to train, skill and support the foster parents so that they can more effectively care for their charges, more so if the children have special needs that require specialised knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In its implementation, there is a need to especially strengthen the coordination and integration of care to ensure the children and young persons receive the better outcomes they deserve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The mission of ensuring a better life for them, however, cannot be left only to the Government and the social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Those of us in the rest of society, whether as neighbours, relatives or volunteers, must join in the efforts to support this effort.

sections.label: Officers needed for extended age
sections.summary: Speaker asks the Minister how many more welfare or probation officers would be needed with the age extension to below 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the extension of the age to below 18, could the Minister share with the House how many more welfare officers or probation officers would be required to cope with the rise in the number of cases to handle such cases?

sections.label: Protections and probationer demographics proposal
sections.summary: The speaker says the measures protect parents and proposes the Probation Service summarise anonymised overaged probationer demographics from the last 12 to 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, all these things I said are meant to protect parents for certain cases in the future under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would also like to propose that the Probation Service provide a summary of the demographics of anonymised potential overaged probationers that the ECPO would have applied in the last 12 to 24 months.

sections.label: Assistance for foster parent caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry would assist caregivers with guidance and financial support, and whether foster parents could get parents' income tax and other benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How would the Ministry assist such caregivers in the given circumstances, from giving guidance to financial support?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that childcare leave would now be extended to foster parents, as, after all, this group of people are playing the similar role as the parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, may I ask if the Ministry would consider extending to this group the income tax and other benefits that are currently available to the parents?

sections.label: Amendments extend coverage to under-18s
sections.summary: The speaker says the amendments extending the Act's coverage to those under 18 are a positive step supporting and protecting more youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, the amendments to the Act that extend coverage to those under 18 is a positive step and will ensure that a greater number of youths are supported and protected.

sections.label: Coverage for emotional and psychological abuse
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill gives more comprehensive coverage to victims of emotional and psychological abuse, with the term "harm" replacing "injury".

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One could recover from the pain of physical abuse yet carry the scar of psychological and emotional trauma for their entire lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that the Bill now provides more comprehensive coverage to protect victims of emotional and psychological abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Changing the term from "injury" to "harm" may seem lexically trivial but it underlies an important shift in how interventions and care could be given.

sections.label: Foster parents recognised as parents
sections.summary: The speaker says foster parents give children and at-risk youths a second chance, and is glad the Bill treats them as parents and grants them childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that foster parents provide children and at-risk youths with a second lease of life and another shot at life that their biological families and parents may not necessarily be able to provide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Bill now also considers them as "parents" and recognises that they provide an important duty of care to the children they foster by according them childcare leave.

sections.label: Foster adoption and caring for youths
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether foster parents may adopt with both parties open and whether biological parents' consent is needed, and urges affective care for young people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would thus like to know if there is the option for foster parents to adopt their foster child, provided both parties are open to the arrangement?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Also, would the biological parents' consent be needed, even if they have shown themselves to be unfit parents through their actions and behaviour which sometimes have been deemed as criminal?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In writing to his fellow Brothers and Educators, de la Salle said: "To deal with young people very harshly is to forego all hope of bringing about any good" and, "have much care and affection for the young people entrusted to you." I believe that it is imperative that we should always display this deep affective care in dealing with our children and young persons, especially those who are at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And we should be helping them not only deal with whatever immediate dangers and challenges they are facing in their lives, but also with the ultimate aim of helping them in the wider context of being able to reintegrate into society.

sections.label: Childcare leave for foster parents
sections.summary: Childcare leave benefits are extended to foster parents to care for foster children who may have been abused, neglected or abandoned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The extension of childcare leave benefits to foster parents to help them care for their foster children who may have been abused, neglected or abandoned recognises the contribution of foster parents and allows for time and flexibility to care for foster children.

sections.label: Unwed mothers maternity leave benefits
sections.summary: In 2017 the Government announced unwed mothers would get the same maternity, childcare and infant leave as married parents, plus Child Development Co-Savings Act benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2017, the Government announced that unwed mothers would be entitled to the same maternity leave, childcare and infant leave as married parents, and enjoy Child Development Co-Savings Act benefits.

sections.label: Unwed mothers buying HDB flats
sections.summary: Unwed mothers can currently buy their own HDB flats only if they are 35 and above, under the Singles Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, unwed mothers can only buy their own HDB flats if they are 35 years old and above, under the Singles Scheme.

sections.label: Tax relief for unwed mothers
sections.summary: There should be tax relief for unwed mothers and foster parents, such as Working Mother's Child Relief and Grandparent Caregiver Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Second, there should be tax relief for unwed mothers and foster parents, such as Working Mother's Child Relief and Grandparent Caregiver Relief.

sections.label: Clarifying emotional harm and abuse
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to give clarity on what constitutes emotional harm or abuse by providing specific circumstances and examples.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: While the concepts of emotional harm, emotional abuse or psychological abuse may seem broad or subjective, what we have sought to do in the Bill is to give as much clarity as we can on what constitutes such harm or abuse, by providing some specific circumstances and then, examples.

sections.label: Financial support for court orders
sections.summary: Asked about financial support for parents complying with Court orders, the response was that no family will be denied services for being unable to afford them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if there is financial support for parents to comply with the orders made by the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will ensure that no family will be denied services because they are unable to afford them.

sections.label: Family-based care for children
sections.summary: Family-based care is preferred for abused or neglected children, with a goal of placing two-thirds in family-based care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Family-based care is preferred as a supportive family environment will help children who have been abused or neglected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: However, 47% of children in out-of-home care are looked after by foster families today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Our goal is to try to place two-thirds of such children in family-based care.

sections.label: Factors deciding child placement
sections.summary: Placement decisions consider the child's age, gender, care needs, foster family availability and children's home profiles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The age, gender as well as the care and intervention needs of each child, availability of foster families, especially those who can care for more than one foster child, and the resident profiles in children's homes, are taken into account when deciding a child's placement.

sections.label: Court conditions for ECPO
sections.summary: The Court must be satisfied of minimum out-of-home care periods, unfit parents and inappropriate return to parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In making an ECPO, the Court must be satisfied that the child has stayed in out-of-home care for at least 12 months in the case of a child who is below three, or at least 24 months for a child aged three and above; the parents are not fit to provide care for the child; and it is not appropriate to return the child to the care and custody of any of his parents.

sections.label: Extended childcare benefits for foster parents
sections.summary: Proposed childcare benefits, if endorsed by Parliament, will give foster parents more time with foster children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The childcare benefits that we are proposing to extend, if this Parliament endorses it, will give them more time to spend with their foster children.

sections.label: Relatives as appointed caregivers
sections.summary: MSF may appoint relatives to care for children, and amended legislation will extend childcare leave to such caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For some children whose parents are unable to provide a safe living environment, MSF may appoint relatives to provide care, similar to how natural parents care for the child.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And the amended legislation will, similarly, extend childcare leave to such appointed caregivers to support them in their caregiving roles.

sections.label: Deadline inserted into CYPA
sections.summary: The amendment inserts a deadline into the CYPA, in line with the Criminal Procedure Code, for handling arrested youth suspects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Our amendment to section 30 of the Act inserts this deadline explicitly into the CYPA itself, in line with section 68 of the Criminal Procedure Code so that there is no ambiguity in how law enforcement officers handle arrested youth suspects.

sections.label: Youth offender discretion and gag orders
sections.summary: Discretion applies to youth offenders with serious or repeat offences, and State Courts can issue gag orders to protect young offenders' identities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked yesterday whether it is a case of discretion or whether it is mandatory when a youth offender has committed or is suspected of having committed serious offences in the Schedule or is a repeat offender, whether or not there is a discretion, the answer is yes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In terms of protecting the identity of young offenders, the State Courts continue to be able to issue gag orders to ensure the identity of the youth is not revealed by the media.

sections.label: Residents assault Auxiliary Police and MSF officers
sections.summary: Seven residents physically assaulted an Auxiliary Police Officer and two MSF officers, causing serious eye and head injuries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Seven residents physically assaulted an Auxiliary Police Officer and two MSF officers, inflicting serious injuries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Auxiliary Police Officer suffered serious eye injury, while the two MSF officers suffered head injuries.

sections.label: KidSTART expansion and parenting programmes
sections.summary: KidSTART has benefited 1,000 children since 2016, will reach 5,000 more, and parenting programmes are available in 292 schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Since KidSTART was piloted in July 2016, 1,000 children from low-income families have benefited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will be expanding KidSTART further – as the Prime Minister had announced at the National Day Rally – to reach another 5,000 children from low-income households over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: MSF has also worked with schools to conduct parenting programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have reached out to 292 schools to make internationally-recognised evidence-based parenting programmes available.

sections.label: Family Guidance Order court mandates
sections.summary: When a parent applies to the Youth Court for a Family Guidance Order, the Court can mandate counselling or treatment for the child or parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Where a parent ultimately decides to apply to the Youth Court for a Family Guidance Order (FGO), the Court can mandate that the child and/or the parents can undergo counselling or any other programme or treatment to protect his well-being.

sections.label: Staggering Bill implementation
sections.summary: Amendments expanding care and protection for children come into force first next year, while raising the Youth Court age limit needs more time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This is why we are staggering the implementation of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We intend to bring into force the amendments to expand care and protection for children first, next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: While we seek to amend the CYPA at this Sitting to raise the age limit of older youths to be tried by the Youth Court, time will be needed to bring these specific amendments into force as various things need to be put into place first.

sections.label: Increase in child abuse cases
sections.summary: Over the past five years, more child abuse and neglect cases have been reported and investigated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In the past five years, we have seen more child abuse and neglect cases being reported and investigated.

sections.label: Youth offender recidivism research
sections.summary: Youth offender recidivism rates have remained stable, and published research covers maltreatment, family profiles and programme evaluations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The overall recidivism rates of our youth offenders have remained stable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have a number of published research papers, covering topics, such as family profiles of maltreated children and the predictors of re-entry into the child protection system in Singapore; impact of childhood maltreatment on recidivism in youth offenders; family characteristics linked to youth offenders in Singapore; evaluation of programmes, such as Functional Family Therapy for youth probationers and Violence Prevention Programme for youth offenders.

sections.label: Bill protects children and youths
sections.summary: The Bill expands coverage to older children, enhances abuse intervention, provides out-of-home care, and helps offending youths reintegrate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, for abused or neglected children, the Bill safeguards their interests by expanding the coverage of the Act to older children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It also enhances our intervention in emotional or psychological abuse cases and provides stable out-of-home care arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, for youths who have committed offences, the Bill would help them ease back into their families and society, and better support them to avoid further offending.

sections.label: Child safety intervention issues
sections.summary: A range of issues may require MSF and social service agencies to intervene for children's safety, across all socio-economic statuses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There is a whole range of issues that may result in MSF and our social service agencies having to intervene to ensure the safety of our children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These cases cut across the whole spectrum of society, regardless of socio-economic status.

sections.label: Staff ratio figure unavailable
sections.summary: The speaker does not have the figure for the staff ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of the staff ratio, I do not have the figure.

sections.label: No hard segregation in homes
sections.summary: Segregation between children in homes for care and protection and for youth offending is not drawn hard and fast.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for whether there is segregation of children who are there for care and protection or there because of youth offending, that line is not drawn hard and fast, because, often, the underlying challenges that result in them having to reside in these homes are similar.

sections.label: Youth guidance officers monitor progress
sections.summary: Youth guidance officers take careful interest in all children in these homes and curtail negative influences as far as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Ultimately, the youth guidance officers take a very clear and careful interest in the progress of all the children who have to be in these homes and ensure that negative influences are curtailed as far as possible.      .
